name: Processor D
justification: Benchmarking on Processor A revealed severe routing bottlenecks: its acyclic tree topology requires 2 SWAPs (+6 CX gates, 100% two-qubit overhead) to execute cross-orbital molecular entangling gates across non-adjacent spin-orbitals, elevating two-qubit depth from 5 to 12. Processor B suffers from degree-5 hub crowding on qubit 6 and a diameter of 4. Processor D resolves these bottlenecks through a 6-qubit chemistry-optimized co-design featuring an all-to-all K4 core on qubits {0,1,2,3} with cross-chords (0,2) and (1,3), eliminating all routing SWAPs (cx_overhead = 0) and minimizing circuit depth for H2 molecular simulation. Error rates are fixed to official standards (p1=0.001, p2=0.005, p_readout=0.01) to isolate architectural connectivity gains. In exchange, Processor D accepts a degree of 4 on bridge nodes 2 and 3, which increases planar control line density and microwave crosstalk risks.
